• Correct Answer: A (Dholavira) - Located on Khadir Bet island in the Rann of Kutch (Gujarat), Dholavira featured an advanced water management network comprising at least 16 rock-cut reservoirs, dams/bunds across the seasonal rivulets Mansar and Manhar, and stone-cut feeder channels.
• Why B is incorrect (Kalibangan): Located in Rajasthan along the dried-up Ghaggar riverbed; best known for the earliest ploughed field, fire altars, and mud-brick fortifications, not stone-built cascade reservoirs.
• Why C is incorrect (Rakhigarhi): Located in Hisar, Haryana; known as the largest Indus Valley site by area with distinct habitation mounds and cemeteries, but lacks an elaborate dam-and-reservoir water-harvesting system.
• Why D is incorrect (Ropar / Rupnagar): Located along the Sutlej in Punjab; known for yielding the first post-independence Harappan excavations and unique dog-buried-with-human grave, without large-scale water-control engineering.
• Often confused with: Lothal (Gujarat), which featured a tidal dockyard connected to the Sabarmati/Bhogavo river for maritime trade, whereas Dholavira managed freshwater harvesting through inland dams and reservoirs.
issues_found: Standard explanations often omit the names of the seasonal streams (Mansar and Manhar) harnessed at Dholavira.
Explanations frequently confuse Lothal's marine dockyard architecture with Dholavira's freshwater reservoir system.
